title: Window functions

spans.text: “Window functions” is a tool for solving a concrete programming problem. Identify the input and desired result, then trace what role the construct plays in the example. Study it not only as syntax, but also for its effects on readability, correctness, resource use, and future changes.
QUESTION: What will this example do? Predict the result first.
Students are numbered within each course by descending score, then student_id.

A window function calculates across related rows without collapsing them into one row as GROUP BY does. PARTITION BY defines groups and ORDER BY defines order within each group. ROW_NUMBER, RANK, and SUM OVER can add row numbers, rankings, or running totals alongside each original row.

Key line: `SELECT student_id, course_id, score,`
What it does: Students are numbered within each course by descending score, then student_id.
Why it is used: Specify the ordering inside OVER and decide how ties should behave.
If omitted or changed: ROW_NUMBER stays unique for tied sort values; RANK gives ties the same rank.
